correctness.rationale: For every n>=1 the finite metric-type classification has disjoint cases x=1,2,3,4 and at most one distance-one leaf, proving the exact F_n formula. The base coefficient sequence b_j is strictly log-concave by 2(n+1)(1+t)^2 > j(n-j)t with t=3*2^(n-j); only the grade-two Turán inequality changes when the extra grade-one term is added. Its exact signed polynomial in 2^n is positive for n=3..10 and negative for all n>=11; n=1,2 have no grade-two condition. The c2-c1 sign and the base tail prove global unimodality. A positive mixture representation proves the total-variation bound. Standalone direct vector enumeration (n<=7) and all-grade exact checks (n<=300) reproduced VERIFY_OK. Finite checks support but do not replace the all-n proof.

value.rationale: The number of named leaves within a fixed short radius is a canonical observable on metric one-point types. The metric star is the simplest finite metric with a distinguished hub and nontrivial leaf-leaf triangle constraints. The theorem completely classifies unimodality and log-concavity over all leaf counts, identifies the first sharp failure and the sole defective grade at every larger size, and shows that failure persists while the normalized law converges exponentially to a binomial distribution in total variation. This supplies a meaningful exact boundary between global approximation and local coefficient regularity, rather than an arbitrary isolated numerical evaluation.
